finalSql:
SELECT cl.claim_id AS clm_id,
       p.policy_id AS polcy_id,
       cl.claim_date::date AS clm_day,
       EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (cl.claim_date - p.effective_date::timestamp)) / 86400 AS days_to_claim,
       CASE
           WHEN p.effective_date = (date_trunc('month', p.effective_date)::date + INTERVAL '1 month - 1 day')::date
           THEN (date_trunc('month', p.effective_date + INTERVAL '6 months') + INTERVAL '1 month - 1 day')::date
           ELSE (p.effective_date + INTERVAL '6 months')::date
       END AS review_dt,
       cl.claim_amount AS clm_amt
FROM claims cl
JOIN policies p ON p.policy_id = cl.policy_id
WHERE cl.claim_date >= TIMESTAMP '2026-03-01'
  AND cl.claim_date < TIMESTAMP '2026-04-01'
ORDER BY cl.claim_amount DESC, cl.claim_id
LIMIT 5

FROM (
    SELECT cl.claim_id AS CLM_ID,
           p.policy_id AS POLCY_ID,
           TRUNC(cl.claim_date)            AS CLM_DAY,
           cl.claim_date - p.effective_date        AS DAYS_TO_CLAIM, (p.effective_date + INTERVAL '6 months')     AS REVIEW_DT,
           cl.claim_amount AS CLM_AMT
    FROM claims cl
    JOIN policies p ON p.policy_id = cl.policy_id
    WHERE TRUNC(cl.claim_date) BETWEEN TO_DATE('2026-03-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD')
                               AND TO_DATE('2026-03-31', 'YYYY-MM-DD')
    ORDER BY cl.claim_amount DESC, cl.claim_id
) AS subquery_1
LIMIT 5

findings.title: Month arithmetic without Oracle's month-end rule
findings.detail: The legacy query uses ADD_MONTHS, which returns the last day of the target month when the start date is the last day of its month (28 Feb + 6 months is 31 Aug). Adding INTERVAL '6 months' keeps the day number (28 Aug). Nothing in this query handles month ends.

proposal.explanation: TRUNC(timestamp) is not a PostgreSQL function, so the claim day is produced with a date cast and the March predicate uses an equivalent half-open timestamp range. Oracle DATE subtraction returns elapsed days, so the timestamp difference is converted from seconds to days. ADD_MONTHS preserves month-end dates, which is explicitly handled for effective dates that are the last day of their month.
changes: Replaced the TRUNC-based March filter with a half-open timestamp range.
Converted claim-date subtraction to elapsed days using EXTRACT(EPOCH) divided by 86400.
Implemented Oracle ADD_MONTHS month-end behavior for the six-month review date.
Used target table and column names while preserving the expected output aliases and ordering.
risks: The numeric display type and formatting of the elapsed-day expression may differ from Oracle even though its value is equivalent.
The expected comparison must treat CLM_DAY as a PostgreSQL date, matching Oracle TRUNC's midnight date value.
